newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Justice Minister Jassan resigns - sources.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Justice Minister Jassan resigns - sources.

text.p: Argentine Justice Minister Elias Jassan has resigned over a scandal involving his contacts with a businessman investigated in the murder of a journalist, government sources said on Tuesday.
President Carlos Menem has offered the post to Argentina's current ambassador to the United States, Raul Granillo Ocampo, one of the sources told Reuters on condition of anonymity.
Jassan told a television programme late on Monday he had "already taken a decision" but that he would wait for Menem to return from a trip to the United States to inform him first.
"That (the resignation) is the decision," one presidential source said on Tuesday.
The scandal snowballed last week after Jassan, who had denied contacts with business tycoon Alfredo Yabran, admitted to having talked to him many times.
Yabran is under investigation for his alleged involvement in the gruesome killing in January of news photographer Jose Luis Cabezas, whose murder has shocked Argentines.
Former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo has accused Yabran of heading a "mafia" with links to the Menem government.
